grounds.point: Section 14(1)(b) requires a post-9 June 1952 subletting, assignment or other parting with possession without the landlord's written consent.
grounds.explanation: The supplied statutory text expressly requires subletting, assignment or other parting with possession without written landlord consent. The reported Parasaram passage confirms the breadth of the possession-transfer limb, including an involuntary sale, but does not itself establish that such a transfer occurred in this target record.

grounds.point: M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd. was carrying on business from the suit premises from 1997 through persons who were also partners of the respondent firm.
grounds.explanation: The respondent stated that Dhian Nath Kapur and Mrs. Anil Kapur were partners of the respondent firm and were carrying on the business of M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd. from the suit property, and the identified bank certificate states that they were directors of that company since 1997. These facts establish company business activity at the premises but do not by themselves establish a transfer of possession.

grounds.point: The respondent surrendered or otherwise parted with possession of the whole or part of the premises to M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd.
grounds.explanation: The petitioner alleged that the respondent was no longer in possession and had sublet the premises to M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd., while the respondent maintained that its own partners remained in possession and continued the respondent's business while also operating the company. The supplied record identifies this as an issue for determination but supplies no target-court finding resolving possession or control, so company operation at the premises cannot be upgraded into a proved parting with possession.

grounds.point: Written landlord consent covering the alleged subletting, assignment or parting with possession is established.
grounds.explanation: The respondent asserted that the original landlord had permitted the Kapur family to induct family members or conduct business under different names, and the record identifies rent and landlord documents from 1964 and 1968. The supplied descriptions do not establish a writing consenting to the alleged 1997 company occupation or other particular transfer, but that evidentiary failure cannot be converted into an affirmative finding that no written consent existed.

grounds.point: The alleged testamentary succession from Dina Nath Kapur to his sons independently establishes an assignment or parting with possession actionable under section 14(1)(b).
grounds.explanation: The respondent pleaded that the business was taken over by Dina Nath Kapur's sons on the basis of his Will, and the petitioner argued that this amounted to parting with possession; the record also identifies later rent acceptance from the respondent firm. The supplied original legal units establish the breadth of section 14(1)(b) in other transfer settings but do not supply a controlling determination of testamentary succession on these facts, while the target court's resolution of this argument is withheld.

reason: The supplied material does not resolve the fixed eviction ground because the decisive factual question of subletting, assignment or parting with possession remains contested, and the existence or absence of the required written consent is not established. The alternative testamentary-transfer theory also remains unresolved within the supplied legal coverage, so either supporting or opposing eviction would require guessing the withheld target reasoning.
